grh_1141b11bc9ebbe158e68.title: A Sense of Pride
paragraphs: After Calvin Black loses his janitorial job, medical bills consume the savings he and his wife Mahalia have left, and the elderly couple is eventually evicted. Too proud to ask for help, they begin living by riding Chicago elevated trains day and night, leaving only for meals and necessities. Their fortunes change when a motorman becomes incapacitated and Calvin fights his way to the controls of a runaway train and brings it to a stop. News coverage reveals both his heroism and the couple's homelessness. The transit authority honors them, job offers pour in, and the Gracious Fellowship they had recently visited promises them a furnished home, restoring both their security and their sense of dignity.

This [[show|sears-radio-theater|Sears Radio Theater]] broadcast aired on June 7, 1979. It is listed as episode 89 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Cecily Tyson, Daws Butler, Gaye Nelson, Helen Martin, and Marvin Miller. Other credited names include Elliott Lewis as director, Elliott Lewis as producer, and Odie Hawkins as writer.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_1131524fe2d83d37c652.title: Violets, Sweet Violets
paragraphs: In Marseille, Harry becomes involved with black-market operator Griffo and a warehouse packed with contraband, including weapons and aircraft parts. An elderly violet seller becomes an unwilling link in the transaction while occupation authorities close in on the network. Harry is arrested and accused of participating in the trade, but offers to clear himself by delivering Griffo and exposing the ring. After tracing Griffo to a boat and subduing him in a violent struggle, Harry turns him over to the authorities. The black-market organization is broken up and Harry is cleared of that charge, although the French prefect strongly suggests that he leave on the next boat.

grh_113c22affc989a450035.title: Words at War 43-10-19 (19) Shortcut to Tokyo
paragraphs: Correspondent Corey Ford describes the largely unseen Aleutian campaign through the men fighting weather and Japanese forces in the fog-bound islands. Patrol crews discover enemy movements, bases are built under brutal conditions and pilots battle an environment that can be as deadly as combat. Ford becomes especially close to pilot Wally, who records a birthday message for his young son before later dying when his plane crashes in the fog. The account ends with new American bases pushing westward through the Aleutians, turning the islands into a possible shortcut toward Japan.

The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.
